recorded.description: Answers of the retired Python capacity command line to these invocations, run from the checkout, recorded before its removal: exit status, standard output and standard error. A {fixture} placeholder stands for the directory holding the files below, which the test writes byte for byte. The modules entry names each Python module that answered and the Git blob of its source at that revision.

cases.stdout:
Sizing a 8-vCPU, 16 GiB host with a 1000 Mbit/s port (reference ceilings measured on an EPYC-class VPS on 2026-09-26; `run` measures yours):

SIMPLESTCHAT_CPUS=7
MEDIA_WORKERS=7
host sysctl: net.core.rmem_max=2097152 net.core.wmem_max=2097152 (the workers ask for 1 MiB socket buffers)
SIMPLESTCHAT_MEMORY_LIMIT=12288m
MAX_CONNECTIONS=800
MAX_ROOMS=800
MAX_PARTICIPANTS_PER_ROOM=800
MAX_BROADCASTERS_PER_ROOM=30
RTC_PORT_END=40006

The app gets 7 CPUs (7 media workers) and 12288 MiB; the rest serves the database, the proxy, TURN and the system.
Meetings of five: about 334 participants (network-bound; 2.39 Mbit/s of egress each, 798 Mbit/s in all).
Webinars: about 800 viewers across the workers (network-bound; one room spreads over every worker).
All-publishing rooms: 25 people, whatever the host: every viewer downloads every tile within the 3 Mbit/s per-viewer cap, which MAX_BROADCASTERS_PER_ROOM=30 keeps in reach; MAX_PARTICIPANTS_PER_ROOM follows the webinar instead.
MAX_CONNECTIONS counts the lightest participants; heavier shapes meet the per-worker CPU guard (0.7 cores) first. SIMPLESTCHAT_MEMORY_LIMIT is the app's share of the host, a process ceiling, not a memory admission guard; monitor RSS and measure the intended workload before raising these estimates.
Open UDP 40000-40006 at the firewall: one port per worker.
Egress is the next wall after CPU: check the provider's quota and price against the Mbit/s above (a full month of meetings at that rate is 262.2 TB).

Meetings of five: about 255 participants (cpu-bound; 2.39 Mbit/s of egress each, 609 Mbit/s in all).
Webinars: about 525 viewers across the workers (cpu-bound; one room spreads over every worker).
All-publishing rooms: 25 people, whatever the host: every viewer downloads every tile within the 3 Mbit/s per-viewer cap, which MAX_BROADCASTERS_PER_ROOM=30 keeps in reach; MAX_PARTICIPANTS_PER_ROOM follows the webinar instead.
MAX_CONNECTIONS counts the lightest participants; heavier shapes meet the per-worker CPU guard (0.7 cores) first. SIMPLESTCHAT_MEMORY_LIMIT is the app's share of the host, a process ceiling, not a memory admission guard; monitor RSS and measure the intended workload before raising these estimates.
Open UDP 40000-40002 at the firewall: one port per worker.
Egress is the next wall after CPU: check the provider's quota and price against the Mbit/s above (a full month of meetings at that rate is 200.2 TB).
A transfer allowance of 5 TB a month is about 4,649 meeting participant-hours or 11,111 webinar viewer-hours: 6 meeting participants or 15 viewers around the clock, and the host's 255 meeting participants use it in 18 hours. Providers usually count both directions, and a meeting participant uploads about as much as they download, so meetings spend it faster than this.
